title: Fixing randomness commutes with execution
statement:
Let $p$ be a public-coin finite-message protocol over a shared-randomness space $\Omega$, private input sets $X$ and $Y$, and output type $\alpha$. Fix a randomness sample $\omega \in \Omega$ and private inputs $x \in X$ and $y \in Y$, and let $p_\omega$ denote the deterministic finite-message protocol obtained from $p$ by substituting $\omega$ for the shared randomness. Then executing $p_\omega$ on $x$ and $y$ yields the same output as the randomized execution of $p$ on $x$ and $y$ with shared randomness $\omega$:
\[
p_\omega.\mathrm{run}(x, y) \;=\; \mathrm{rrun}(p, x, y, \omega).
\]
replaced:
For any inputs $x : X$ and $y : Y$, the deterministic run of
$p.\mathrm{toDeterministic}\,\omega$ equals the randomised run at $\omega$:
$(p.\mathrm{toDeterministic}\,\omega).\mathrm{run}\,x\,y = p.\mathrm{rrun}\,x\,y\,\omega$.
